title: How do you rig animations onto bulky, stylized characters?
author: Equal_Guarantee_6397
selftext:
I'm building a game with bulky characters (big shoulders, oversized hands) that don't fit typical humanoid proportions.

I've tried using stock and mocap animations on them. They look fine on the original character, but once I retarget them onto mine, the shoulders hunch, the arms bend at weird angles, and the hands phase through the body.

How do you handle this? Do you fix the rig, use a different retargeter, is it a problem with the animation itself, or do I just have to hand-key on the character?

comments.author: VictorBuildsApps
comments.body:
Before hand-keying I'd check the rig, because on my generated characters a lot of the arm and shoulder trouble turned out to be skin weights, not the clips.

Across the five generated bodies in one of my games, the automatic skin weights put some parts on the wrong bone, and it didn't show up at rest or in low-arm clips: pauldrons and a gorget weighted to the head, sleeves carrying clavicle and spine weight down to the elbow. On one bow draw, a sleeve with up to 0.43 of that torso weight stayed 6-7 cm back up the arm as it rose, and the elbow opened between sleeve and bracer. What found them was a per-clip check for mesh edges stretched past 2.5x their rest length and 4 cm, grouped by which two bones the vertices mostly follow. A clavicle/head pair is a wrong-bone weight, not cloth.

The fix isn't universal either. Moving the sleeve weight onto the arm crumpled one character's elbow plate and made another's big gauntlet worse at the shoulder, so those two didn't get that rule.

For hands going through the body, I'd measure instead of eyeballing. My pipeline checks which body vertices a held prop touches on every frame after a clip change, since a low IK error says nothing about clearance. A similar check of the hand mesh against the torso might show where yours go in.

And I don't key from scratch: retarget, then fix on top in layers.
